items.title: Law Student moves Supreme Court alleging UP govt misled court, no action taken against Executive Magistrate who issued notice over CJP protest
items.summary: Law student Akshat Tripathi has moved the Supreme Court alleging that the Uttar Pradesh government misled the court on the action taken over the Rs 5 lakh bond notice issued to him in connection with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest. His writ petition was mentioned on September 10 before a Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, which is hearing petitions arising out of the July protests at Jantar Mantar and other parts of the country. On that day, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, on instructions from the State of UP, told the Court that the notice was issued not by the District Magistrate but by the Executive Magistrate, and that the official responsible had been suspended. "It was not the District Magistrate. It was some other official who has been suspended," Mehta had said, adding, "Let's not sensationalise it." In the fresh application, Tripathi has relied on an Indian Express report which states that UP DGP Headquarters later clarified that only Sub-Inspector Shiva Pandey, whose report formed the basis of the notice, was suspended. items.title: Veeramani POCSO case: Directors Vetrimaaran, Ameer demand thorough probe
items.summary: Directors Vetrimaaran and Ameer issued a joint statement on Sunday, September 27, condemning the alleged sexual abuse of minor girls by Gem Granites chairman R Veeramani and called for an impartial investigation without any pressure. The directors said the crimes against the girls were “shocking” and “unforgivable” and demanded that everyone who attempted to protect Veeramani be thoroughly investigated and punished under the law. They also called for the survivors to be provided with legal and psychological counselling and social rehabilitation, while stressing that their identities and dignity must be protected. Addressing criticism that they had remained silent on the issue until now, Vetrimaaran and Ameer said in their statement: “Whoever commits sexual offences, our voice will always be raised against them.” They also called for stringent punishment for sexual offenders without any concessions and said the Special Investigation Team (SIT) investigating the Veeramani case should conduct its probe honestly and without being subjected to pressure. items.title: ‘Why are our films denied screening?’ Filmmakers at Kerala docu film fest ask
items.summary: Standing in a group at the Kairali Theatre complex in Thiruvananthapuram, wearing black and looking dejected, are filmmakers and crew members of some of the films that were not allowed screening at the International Documentary and Short Film Festival of Kerala (IDSFFK) this year. They are hoping to meet the newly appointed chairperson of the Kerala Chalachitra Academy, actor Ravindran, to present their case. No reason has been given for not allowing the screening of eight films, including five in the competition section, at the IDSFFK. The Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting had initially denied censor exemption to 31 films selected at the fest, but after the government of Kerala wrote seeking permission, 23 of these were approved . “We hope to meet the chairperson and ask for an explanation on why our films were denied approval. The IDSFFK is very important for us, and two of my previous films have won awards at the festival.
